facts.value: Paper Table 3 prints £340,000k of PWLB long-term at 2.38% weighted plus £280,092k of mixed Local authorities/PWLB short-term at 3.64% weighted, totalling £620,092k at 2.95% (Appendix C p.4). Our PWLB price book at 31 March 2026 shows 11 loans totalling £400,000,000 at a weighted 2.2538%. The £340m long-term line ties to our file on principal.

source.title: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Table 3 (p.4) does not split PWLB from LA in the short-term row (labelled 'Local authorities / PWLB (short-term)'). Our £400m of PWLB reconciles to £340m long-term (matches paper first row on principal; weighted 2.38% is 0.13 above our overall 2.25% — consistent with excluding a £60m tail of near-maturity PWLB at ~1.68%) plus ~£60m of PWLB inside the £280m short-term line. The residual ~£220m in the short-term row is LA temp borrowing at an implied ~4.17%, inside the 4.0-7.0% range narrated on p.4. Reconciliation is close and directionally consistent; the £340m principal number ties exactly.

facts.value: General Fund CFR £622,927k (31.03.25) → £647,969k (31.03.26), movement £25,042k. Total borrowing £585,316k → £620,092k, movement £34,776k. Internal borrowing £37,611k → £27,877k, movement (£9,734k).

source.title: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Table 1 (p.3). Balance-sheet identity ties exactly: 647,969 − 620,092 − 0 = 27,877. Table 1 does not print an OLTL line; Appendix D shows £2,000k OLTL for 2025/26 authorised-limit purposes but the identity ties only with actual OLTL at zero. The £2m in Appendix D is headroom in the limit, not a live liability.

facts.value: Internal borrowing £27,877k at 31 March 2026, down from £37,611k a year earlier. 4.3% of CFR is carried internally.

source.title: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Table 1 (p.3). Verbatim narrative p.3: 'The Authority pursued its strategy of keeping borrowing and investments below their underlying levels, sometimes known as internal borrowing, in order to reduce risk and keep interest costs low.' 27,877/647,969 = 4.30% — nearly all CFR is externally funded. Compare Appendix D's Liability Benchmark line (620,653 for 25/26) sitting £562k below gross borrowing (620,091), which is what a near-fully-externalised book looks like.

facts.value: Under 12 months bucket at 44% (£272.8m implied) against a 50% upper limit; 12-24m at 10%, 24m-5y at 23%, 5-10y at 0%, 10-25y at 23% (Appendix C p.7).

source.title: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: The '25 years and above' row is printed as 100% actual, which is inconsistent — the bucket percentages add to 200%. Reading it as 0% (consistent with the p.7 narrative 'In 25/26 this maturity length has been between 1 - 5 years') makes the buckets sum to exactly 100%. Treat the printed 100% as a paper anomaly; do not repeat it in outreach. Under-12m at 44% against a 50% limit is what's material — only 6 percentage points of headroom on the short bucket.

facts.value: CFR £647,969k Actual 25/26 → £711,577k Est 26/27 → £774,534k Est 27/28 → £841,214k Est 28/29 (Appendix D). Gross borrowing forecast 620,091 → 683,700 → 746,656 → 813,336 across the same years — increment of £193,245k over three years.

source.title: Appendix D — Prudential Indicators Q4 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Appendix D 'Annual change in capital financing requirement (CFR)' row: 24,785 / 63,609 / 62,956 / 66,680 (25/26 uses a different working file than Appendix C Table 1 which shows CFR movement of 25,042 for 25/26; £257k mismatch across the two appendices, internal-only). The incremental borrowing gets priced against the current curve (5-yr certainty 5.34%, 10-yr 5.83% at 14 Aug 2026, notice 314/26 PM), not against the book's 2.95% blended rate.

facts.value: Proportion of financing costs (Interest + MRP) to net revenue stream: 123% Actual 25/26, rising 120% (26/27) → 135% (27/28) → 140% (28/29). Income from non-treasury investments to net revenue stream: 124% Actual 25/26, rising to 137% by 28/29 (Appendix D).

source.title: Appendix D — Prudential Indicators Q4 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.value: Security of Commercial and Housing Investments 2025/26 Actual: (£27,027k) — negative, i.e. debt exceeds the accounting valuation of the commercial investment portfolio by £27m. Yield of Commercial Property Investment Income 5.65% (25/26 Actual), 5.53% (26/27 Est); Commercial Property Reserve £3,162k (25/26) drawn down to £452k (26/27) and £0 (27/28 onwards). Non-treasury investment income as a proportion of Usable Reserves 63% (25/26) → 78% (26/27) (Appendix D).

source.title: Appendix D — Prudential Indicators Q4 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Margin note verbatim: 'The indicator shows the security of the Council's assets by comparing the accounting valuation to the debt outstanding.' Negative means the accounting valuation of the commercial and housing investment portfolio is £27m less than the debt attributed to it — an unrealised revaluation loss. Not a treasury topic per EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §5 (commercial property findings are out of scope for first contact; discount-finding-must-never-become-advice). The Commercial Property Reserve running from £3.2m to zero across three years is worth noting for future contact once a relationship exists, but not in a cold email.

facts.value: Total treasury investments £24,751k at 31.03.26 (from £21,601k), yielding 3.78% weighted. Split: banks & building societies (unsecured) £1,251k at 1.35%; Money Market Funds £13,500k at 3.85%; Pooled Funds £8,801k at 4.00% (Table 4, Appendix C p.5). £8.6m held in CCLA Local Authorities' Property Fund (p.5 narrative).

source.title: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Table 4 has a £1,199k constant discrepancy — the three category rows sum to £20,402k opening and £23,552k closing but the total print is £21,601k opening and £24,751k closing. Same gap at both dates — a category is missing from the row split. Do not use Table 4 splits externally; use Table 2 aggregates only. Table 5 confirms CCLA (Non Specified Investments) at £8.8m against £10m limit. The 2029 override cliff applies to the £8.8m CCLA holding — worth mentioning as a training angle in outreach.

facts.value: All treasury indicators complied for 2025/26 per Chief Finance Officer sign-off (Appendix C p.6). Debt actual £620,092k against Operational Boundary £637,902k and Authorised Limit £647,902k (Table 6). Any-single-organisation limit £10m/£10m/£10m (max=limit, complied). MMF limit £10m/£10m/£10m (max=limit, complied). CCLA £8.8m against £10m.

source.title: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Compliance limits vs Appendix D show £67k mismatches on Op Boundary (637,902 vs 635,969+2,000=637,969) and Authorised Limit (647,902 vs 645,969+2,000=647,969) — different working files. Internal-only. Two limits printed at maximum-equals-limit is inside the rules, not a breach; noted for the file so we don't over-read as compliance stress.

facts.value: Liability Benchmark 620,653 (25/26 Actual) → 681,882 (26/27) → 754,502 (27/28) → 826,579 (28/29) £'000. Gross borrowing forecast 620,091 / 683,700 / 746,656 / 813,336 across the same years. External borrowing sits £562k below LB for 25/26, £1,818k above in 26/27, then £7,846k below in 27/28 and £13,243k below in 28/29.

source.title: Appendix D — Prudential Indicators Q4 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Margin note verbatim: 'An alternative strategy, showing the lowest risk level of borrowing.' Small sub-LB position in the outer years means the plan is to run down investment balances modestly rather than fully externalise the CFR. That is consistent with the p.3 narrative on internal borrowing. Worth noting: Eastleigh already prints the LB indicator in its statutory report, which is ahead of many councils and matters given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Code updates.

facts.value: PWLB certainty rate movement over 2025/26 (Appendix C p.7): Bank Rate 4.50% → 3.75%; 1-yr 4.82% → 5.04%; 5-yr 4.94% → 5.28%; 10-yr 5.38% → 5.72%; 20-yr 5.88% → 6.23%; 50-yr 5.63% → 6.08%. Short-term LA borrowing rates 4.0-4.5% for most of the year, rising to 5.0-7.0% by year-end (p.4).

source.title: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Cabinet, 16 July 2026

facts.note: Move from THEIR year-end reference (31 March 2026) to today (14 Aug 2026 notice 314/26 PM): 1-yr 5.04% → 4.95% (-0.09); 5-yr 5.28% → 5.34% (+0.06); 10-yr 5.72% → 5.83% (+0.11); 20-yr 6.23% → 6.38% (+0.15). Short end drifted lower, long end 6-15bp higher since year-end. Do not use 'roughly 0.6% higher' — that's the move from Feb strategy dates, not from 31 March 2026 outturns.

facts.value: Indicative discount on the 10 live PWLB loans as at 14 August 2026 (notice 314/26 PM): balance £370,000,000; settlement £290,990,595; net discount £79,009,405 (21.4% of principal). 8 loans below par, 2 above. Largest discounts: PW509118 £90m at 2.20% (mat 2069-04-02) −£48.246m; PW505983 £50m at 2.31% (mat 2067-04-07) −£25.709m.

source.title: PWLBtoday break-cost engine (monitor/outreach/canon_break_cost.py) using EASTLEIGH BOROUGH COUNCIL loan-book snapshot and DMO premature-repayment curve notice 314/26 PM

Discount applies to our £370m live PWLB slice; nothing about LA borrowing (which forms the balance of the £280m short-term line in Table 3). officer.body:
Hi,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's premature-repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 that went to Cabinet on 16 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A reconciliation first. Table 3 (p.4 of Appendix C) prints £340m of long-term PWLB at a weighted 2.38%, plus £280m of mixed local-authority and PWLB short-term at 3.64%. Our PWLB file at 31 March 2026 holds 11 loans totalling £400m at 2.25% weighted. The £340m long-term line ties to our file on principal; the 0.13 percentage-point gap on rate is consistent with excluding a ~£60m tail of near-maturity PWLB sitting inside your short-term line at around 1.7%, which is what our two under-12-months loans at 1.655% look like. Balance-sheet identity ties to the pound: your CFR of 647,969 less external borrowing 620,092 less other long-term liabilities zero equals internal borrowing 27,877, which is what Table 1 prints.

What's most distinctive in the file is the value of the long-term anchor. Priced against today's certainty curve (14 August, notice 314/26 PM) the ten live loans on our file carry an indicative discount of £79m against £370m of principal — roughly 21% below par. Two long-dated loans do most of the work: £90m maturing April 2069 at 2.20%, and £50m maturing April 2067 at 2.31%, together carrying about £74m of that discount. That is what borrowing at 2.20% locks in against a 5.83% ten-year certainty curve today. Every council's book is priced daily on this basis at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis — the same engine and the same DMO curve. Indicative only, of course, and only the DMO can quote; we model no MRP or accounting treatment on top.

The other feature worth naming is the forward path. Appendix D projects the CFR from £648m today to £841m by 2028/29 — roughly £193m of incremental borrowing over three years. That drawdown gets priced against the current curve rather than the 2.95% blended rate of today's book. Today's 5-year certainty is 5.34% and 10-year is 5.83%; on £193m at 5-year that is roughly £10m a year of extra interest once fully drawn. Alongside that, the maturity structure at p.7 puts 44% of the current book under 12 months against a 50% upper limit — the short end reprices most of the year regardless of what incremental borrowing costs. The rate curve and the SONIA path it runs off are at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard.

One small piece of context from the wider file. July's sector PWLB drawings across all councils were £368m from just 19 borrowers — a thin month. The breakdown by tenor and by council is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity. It gives a sense of what shape of borrowing has been going through and what the sector has been paying since the outturn was set. On our side we hold PWLB only, so if you have any LOBO, bank or market debt outside PWLB none of the above touches it.

Four courses fit. Reading the PWLB certainty curve covers the mechanics of what your paper quotes at p.4. Liability Benchmark: the essentials is worth watching given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Code updates — Appendix D already prints the LB line and your external borrowing sits within £562k of it, which is ahead of many. IFRS 9 statutory override — the 2029 cliff matters given the CCLA holding on p.6 of Appendix C. And Members' introduction to treasury is the one to point Cabinet members at ahead of the next strategy cycle. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Sources: Appendix C — Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26, and Appendix D — Prudential Indicators Q4 2025/26, Cabinet, 16 July 2026 (Eastleigh.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s50043556, s50043557).
